verified_independently: Read sky/schwarzschild.gdshaderinc line by line against physics/schwarzschild.gd (regular_part, _texel_lerp, _rows_cr, catmull_rom, row_coordinate, fwd_column): rule 1 (one fractional column for all rows, carried as (i0,f)), rule 2 (sine-ratio form is algebraically the cot(psi/2) weight; checked by hand), rule 3 (ghost points 2p1-p2 / 2p2-p1, j1 clamped to N_ROWS-2) are all mirrored. The weak branch (small-angle root, rationalised for F<0, Newton on the first-order map, dF/dpsi = 1 + k/(2 sin^2(psi/2))) is correct.
lens_fwd header: G = central difference of R + d/dx of the ln-tanh singular part, so the shader's radial mip term |1 - G/dpsi| is the full d delta/dx; no missing singular term.
Order-1 material receives every later uniform: all starfield setters go through _parameter(), which loops extra_materials. Ring flag is bit 64 and catalogue flag bits are 1..16 (no collision).

Renders read (renders/bh_sky/small): mw_r5_toward_hover (black centred shadow, nested lensed Milky Way, thin photon ring), ring_r10 (thin uniform white Einstein ring around the shadow, no blobs), grid_r3_toward_hover (nested grid arcs, Einstein-cross lobes on the horizon, black shadow). Physically plausible.

findings.detail: InteriorSky.apply() runs every sim frame and GrLens.set_gr() then runs the whole of _select() (a GDScript loop over every cone candidate: direction_to allocation, angle, flux, sort_custom) plus _upload_ring() twice (set_gr, then set_exposure), plus a ring_cones() recompute (about 200 table-based image() calls) and a column-texture rebuild whenever r changes. I measured it at the large tier (335,189 stars, r=10 toward the galactic centre, 3698 candidates, 64 ring stars, 418 overflow): set_gr takes a median 2.4 ms with r static and 3.1 ms (max 3.4) with r changing, on the M4 Max, on top of the 8 ms frame. The bench's GR-on sweep calls set_gr once and then only moves the camera, so it never exercises this per-frame path. The as-built text 'the sweep ... ~1 ms per frame' and 'holds 60 fps with margin' omit it. Still inside 16.7 ms on this machine, but it is unmeasured on slower hardware, and it grows with the candidate count (hole toward the dense bulge).
findings.suggestion: Skip _select()/_upload_ring() in set_gr unless the cones, the candidate set, the exposure or the ring membership inputs actually changed (h moved > REFRESH_RAD, r changed > 1e-4 r, catalogue/ship key changed); drop the duplicate _upload_ring on the set_exposure path when the exposure is unchanged. Add a bench variant that calls InteriorSky.set_gr every frame with a decreasing r, and report that p50/p99. Correct the as-built sentence to include the measured per-frame set_gr cost.

findings.detail: The mutation kills (x-linear weight, repeated end row p0, p3) are claimed in the commit, JSON and design notes, but no mutation switch exists in the tree, so a reviewer cannot reproduce them and nothing in CI would notice if GR10/GR11 were later weakened (for example the 2e-5 tolerance or the radii set). The GR10/GR11 goldens themselves are real (per-pixel shader float32 vs CPU, worst 0.33 of the limit) and I re-ran them green.
findings.suggestion: Add a debug uniform (gr_mutant, 0 in play, like gr_probe) selecting the three mutants and a make target or GR_ONLY mode that asserts GR10/GR11 FAIL for each, or record the mutant diffs and observed worst ratios in the as-built note so the claim can be re-checked.

findings.detail: Two checks are weak. (a) 'shader weight form ... = the cot weight' only proves a trigonometric identity in GDScript; it does not touch the shader. The real guard is GR10. (b) 'uniforms: gr_dg is the state's blueshift; the hole is galactic +x = world -Z' adds the value and a distance into one number, so a compensating pair of errors could pass.
findings.suggestion: Check gr_dg and the gr_h distance as two separate assertions; keep the identity test but label it as a derivation check, not a shader check.

findings.detail: No guard for r < 2 (row clamps to the r=2 row) or for a state whose shadow is missing or non-finite; the shader would then divide by a bad alpha. The sim keeps r >= 2 at present, but the M3.4 contract is not asserted here. The ring-star candidate sweep also lags a new state by up to count/CHUNK frames (about 34 at the large tier), during which newly in-cone stars draw as splats with mu capped at 8; this is documented only implicitly.
findings.suggestion: Clamp or reject r < 2 and non-finite shadow in GrLens.set_gr (treating it as GR off, with a push_warning). State the sweep latency in the as-built note, or run refresh_now() on the first frame of a new hole.
